evals.name: top-candidates-team-meeting
evals.prompt: we've got the parkinsons evidence base built out in this repo — what are the most promising drugs to repurpose? i need to bring 2-3 concrete suggestions to our team meeting thursday and actually be able to defend them
evals.expected_output: Novel candidates only (not already-approved PD drugs), each with target/action, direction rationale, toxin+pathway evidence, and a stated failure mode. Should note the already-approved PD drugs as pipeline validation rather than proposals.
assertions: Proposes at least 2 specific named drug candidates
Proposals exclude drugs already approved/used in PD (rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, rivastigmine, donepezil, methylphenidate)
Explains that already-approved PD drugs ranking highly is pipeline validation, not a proposal
Gives the molecular target and direction of action for each proposed candidate
States a specific failure mode or weakness for each proposed candidate
Cites concrete numbers (q-value, trial count, or toxin count) rather than adjectives alone
Flags that the cohort is a narrow slice (71 drugs from 30 targets from 10 toxins), not a comprehensive PD screen

evals.name: sanity-check-risk-drug
evals.prompt: someone on the team is pushing hard for capivasertib for the PD program because AKT1 came up in our target list. can you sanity check that before i have to give an opinion
evals.expected_output: Identifies capivasertib as mechanistic_risk: it inhibits AKT1, a pro-survival pathway that rotenone/MPTP already suppress, so it pushes the same direction as the toxin. Should recommend against and explain the direction logic.
assertions: Recommends against capivasertib for the PD program
Identifies it as a mechanistic risk / wrong-direction hypothesis rather than a weak candidate
Explains that inhibiting AKT1 pushes the same direction as rotenone/MPTP suppression of pro-survival signalling
Names the protective direction (AKT activation) or otherwise states what would be needed instead
Does not suggest capivasertib merely needs more supporting evidence to proceed

evals.name: explain-etanercept-skeptic
evals.prompt: I need to explain to our neurologist collaborator why etanercept keeps coming out near the top of our parkinsons list. she's skeptical of anything that came out of a computational pipeline so i need the actual mechanistic argument plus whatever the weak points are
evals.expected_output: TNF inhibition rationale with toxin/pathway evidence and real numbers, plus the blood-brain-barrier weakness (biologic modality, IgG <1% of serum in CSF) surfaced honestly. Ideally offers an evidence graph.
assertions: Gives the TNF-inhibition mechanistic rationale for PD
Surfaces the blood-brain-barrier limitation of etanercept as a large molecule/biologic
Cites concrete evidence numbers (pathway q-value, toxin count, or trial counts)
Names which environmental toxins implicate TNF
Provides or offers an evidence graph / diagram
States that the database contains no PD efficacy data for this drug
